To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the immunogenicity of a synthetic hapten is largely influenced by the location and length of the spacer arm; 2) the immunogen structure is a crucial parameter for the generation of highly-specific antibodies; 3) the antibody-antibody interaction can be profiled according to their recognition pattern; 4) antibodies with equivalent affinity for forchlorfenuron are obtained from different derivatives; and 5) the antibody structure is a crucial factor for the recognition of for

the antibody response against forchlorfenuron can be modulated by the immunogen structure and that the epitopes recognized by the elicited antibodies are dependent upon both the haptenic scaffold and the spacer length.

(1) antibodies can be raised against forchlorfenuron with high affinity and selectivity; (2) the immunogen design has a major impact on the antibody repertoire; (3) the antibody-antibody relationships can be successfully described by a hierarchical clustering analysis; (4) the antibody-epitope relationships can be established by means of a hierarchical clustering of the immunogen structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and efficient approach to obtain high-affinity monoclonal antibodies for the detection and quantification of forchlorfenuron.
the design of immunogens and the development of a new strategy for the characterization of the resulting antibodies.
the design, synthesis and immunogenicity of a series of novel haptens for the production of highly selective and sensitive antibodies against the synthetic plant regulator forchlorfenuron.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunogen structure has a significant impact on the resulting antibody properties.

the immunization of rabbits with the most hydrophilic and least bulky derivatives, bearing the haptenic moiety at the C-2 position, was the best strategy to raise antibodies with high affinity and selectivity towards forchlorfenuron.
the antibody-antibody interaction is a highly valuable tool for the development of new immunosensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunogen design is crucial for the generation of high affinity and selective binders, but it should be accompanied by a thorough characterization of the antibody repertoire.
the use of forchlorfenuron mimicking haptens is a promising approach for the production of highly selective antibodies.
the design and selection of immunogens is a key step in the development of immunoassays for the detection of small molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of haptens with a high number of functional groups and a flexible spacer allows the production of antibodies with high affinities and specificities.
the use of a library of immunogens, with different chemical features, is a promising strategy for the generation of a panel of highly selective and sensitive antibodies for forchlorfenuron.
the immunogen design is critical for the generation of antibodies that recognize the desired epitope.
